chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “It is appropriate for one who recites the Qur'an, when he passes by a verse in the Qur'an containing a request or a warning, to ask at that point for the best of what he hopes for, and to ask for well-being and safety from the Fire and from the punishment.”

key_terms.الْعَافِيَةَ: well-being, safety, and protection from harm
key_terms.الْقُرْآنَ: the Qur'an being recited and reflected upon
key_terms.تَخْوِيفٌ: a warning that instills fear of punishment
key_terms.خَيْرَ: the best good that one hopes to receive
key_terms.مَسْأَلَةٌ: a passage involving asking for something or prompting supplication

ai.seo_question: What should a person say when reciting Qur'an and passing verses of warning or request?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the etiquette of engaging with the Qur'an during recitation. When a reciter encounters verses of promise or warning, he should respond with du'a, asking Allah for the good he hopes for and seeking protection from the Fire and punishment.
